definition: The practice of training a model across multiple GPUs, TPUs, or machines simultaneously to handle models or datasets too large for a single device.
details: Distributed training strategies include data parallelism (splitting the data across devices), model parallelism (splitting the model itself), and pipeline parallelism, often combined for training the largest LLMs.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Distributed Training — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
